note: SEALED HOLDOUT-3 — §5e/§5h. Grammars mined from market + thruline (A37) and provenance-trap families mined from the real corpus (A46 mining table, M3.12.1). Content is synthetic per A22: the grammar is real, every number, name and path is invented. Sealed BEFORE any M3.12.2 classifier or renderer change; opened exactly once at M3.12.3.
api_contract: Each case carries `provenance` ∈ {executed_output, command_source, prose_context}. The harness must classify through the provenance-aware entry point. command_source and prose_context cases MUST abstain BY CONSTRUCTION (§5g), not by string inspection — a classifier that only passes them because their wording happens to look unusual has not implemented the rule. executed_output traps are the second line: modality guards, quoted shell source, §5f ambiguity, and the A37 ratio rules.

manifest._rule: §5h: asserted against contents by tests/sealed_manifests.rs at seal time.

gate: real-format coverage ≥ 70% · trap misclassifications = 0 · abstentions allowed on real cases. A trap that parses, or any wrong count, fails outright.

cases.grammar: executed output: `cat` of a shell script containing printf
cases.defence: §5g: quoted shell source inside a result is source, not output — the holdout-2 trap-3 shape.
cases.text:
ok=$((ok+1))
  printf 'FINAL: %d pass, %d fail\n' "$ok" "$bad"
  exit $rc

cases.grammar: executed output: `cat` of a harness defining PASS/FAIL helpers
cases.defence: §5g: quoted shell source inside a result is source, not output — the holdout-2 trap-3 shape.
cases.text:
good() { printf 'PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
bad()  { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
